title: Distributed Job Scheduler
summary: A distributed job scheduler is cron for thousands of machines. It must fire each job once, on time, even when scheduler nodes crash, and recover cleanly when workers die mid-job. The usual design is a single leader, chosen by a lease, that creates one uniquely keyed run per scheduled time, a queue that hands runs to workers on a timed lease, and heartbeats that let stuck runs be retried.

walkthrough.title: Define a job
walkthrough.text: A team registers nightly-invoices: cron 0 2 * * * in UTC, a 2-hour timeout, up to 3 retries, and a policy for missed runs.

walkthrough.title: Elect a leader
walkthrough.text: Several scheduler replicas compete for a lease row in the job store. Only the holder schedules, and it must renew the lease every few seconds or another replica takes over.

walkthrough.title: Create due runs exactly once
walkthrough.text: Each tick, the leader finds jobs whose next fire time has passed and inserts a run keyed by (job_id, scheduled_time). The unique key means a crashed and restarted leader cannot create the same run twice.

walkthrough.title: Enqueue the run
walkthrough.text: The run is placed on a ready queue with its priority and concurrency group, so at most one nightly-invoices run executes at a time.

walkthrough.title: Worker leases the run
walkthrough.text: A worker claims the run with a visibility timeout. If the worker disappears, the lease expires and the run becomes available again.

walkthrough.title: Heartbeat and complete
walkthrough.text: The worker heartbeats while running, extending its lease, then reports success or failure with logs and duration to the run history.

walkthrough.title: Retry, alert, catch up
walkthrough.text: Failed or timed-out runs retry with exponential backoff. After the final attempt the owner is alerted. Runs missed while the system was down are run once or skipped, per the job's policy.

data.label: Job Definitions

input.name: Status
input.type: Run history, next fire time, failures

output.name: Job
output.type: { name, cron, tz, timeout, retries, catchup }

responsibilities: Declare what runs, when, and how failures are handled.
Make jobs idempotent so a retry is safe.

failureModes.scenario: Cron in local time across a DST change
failureModes.impact: Job runs twice or not at all that night.
failureModes.mitigation: Schedule in UTC or use DST-aware rules explicitly.
Pass the run ID; jobs deduplicate work by it.

data.label: Scheduler (Leader)

output.name: Runs
output.type: INSERT run (job, scheduled_time) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

responsibilities: Is the only replica creating runs at any moment.
Computes next fire times from cron expressions.
Hands runs to the queue and advances schedules.

failureModes.scenario: Leader pauses (GC) past its lease, then resumes
failureModes.mitigation: Fencing token on writes; the unique run key absorbs duplicates.

failureModes.impact: Thundering herd on workers and downstream systems.
failureModes.mitigation: Add jitter to schedules; per-group concurrency limits.

data.label: Job & Run Store

input.name: Writes
input.type: Lease renewals, new runs, state changes

responsibilities: Holds definitions, the leader lease, and every run's state.
Guarantees one run per job per scheduled time.
Keeps history for audit and debugging.

failureModes.mitigation: HA database; catch-up policy when it returns.

data.label: Ready Queue

input.name: Runs
input.type: Ready runs with priority + concurrency key

output.name: Leases
output.type: Run handed to one worker for N minutes

responsibilities: Delivers each run to one worker at a time.
Makes runs available again if a lease expires.

failureModes.impact: A second worker starts the same run.
failureModes.mitigation: Heartbeats extend the lease; size timeouts to the job.
Autoscale workers on queue depth and age.

data.label: Worker Pool
responsibilities: Heartbeats while running so stuck runs are detectable.

failureModes.scenario: Worker hangs but heartbeats keep going
failureModes.mitigation: Hard timeouts enforced by the platform, not just the worker.

data.label: Run Monitor & Alerts

output.name: Actions
output.type: Retry with backoff, alert owner, mark failed

responsibilities: Detects failed, timed-out, and missed runs.
Alerts owners when a job keeps failing or did not run.

failureModes.mitigation: Alert on 'expected run did not complete by time X'.

failureModes.scenario: Retry storm against a broken dependency
failureModes.mitigation: Exponential backoff with jitter and retry caps.
